_comment: MRKH's candidate gene WNT4 is NOT fully confirmed - most MRKH patients have no identified WNT4 mutation, and this is explicitly noted below rather than asserted as a settled fact. Anatomy edges use Hetionet's real DlA ('localizes') metaedge rather than a generic 'associates' label, since Hetionet has no Disease-associates-Anatomy metaedge. No approved pharmacological treatment exists (management is surgical/psychological), so no Compound-treats-Disease edge is added.

node.name: Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser syndrome
node.notes: Congenital absence/hypoplasia of the uterus and upper two-thirds of the vagina (Mullerian agenesis) in individuals with a typical female karyotype (46,XX). Not present in Hetionet v1.0's 137-disease set.

supporting_nodes.name: WNT4
supporting_nodes.notes: CANDIDATE gene, not a confirmed monogenic cause. WNT4 variants have been reported in only a small subset of MRKH cases (some associated with a hyperandrogenism variant), and most individuals with MRKH have no identified WNT4 mutation. Included here as an evidence-based candidate association, explicitly flagged as unconfirmed rather than causal.

supporting_nodes.name: uterus
supporting_nodes.notes: Reused directly from Hetionet v1.0 (already present as UBERON:0000995).

supporting_nodes.name: vagina
supporting_nodes.notes: Reused directly from Hetionet v1.0 (already present as UBERON:0000996).

edges.evidence: UNCONFIRMED / candidate association only. WNT4 sequence variants have been reported in a minority of MRKH cases in the literature; causality is not established for the majority of patients, most of whom have no WNT4 mutation. This edge should be treated as lower-confidence than the Wilson's/SCA3 gene edges.
MRKH is defined by congenital uterine agenesis/hypoplasia.
MRKH also involves aplasia of the upper two-thirds of the vagina.

deliberately_omitted.compound_treats_disease: No approved pharmacological treatment exists. Standard management is surgical (e.g. vaginal dilation therapy, neovaginoplasty) and psychological support - not a disease-modifying compound therapy in the sense Hetionet's CtD edges represent.
